slides.alt_text: The BSB text of Gen 12:7: Then the LORD appeared to Abram and said, ‘I will give this land to your offspring.’
slides.body: “Then the LORD appeared to Abram and said, ‘I will give this land to your offspring.’”
slides.heading: Gen 12:7

slides.alt_text: Slide one introduces Paul's singular-offspring argument about Christ.
slides.body: Genesis promises land to Abraham's ‘offspring.’ Paul says Scripture did not say ‘offsprings’ but one ‘offspring’—Christ. It sounds like a grammatical prediction. Is it?
slides.heading: Does one ‘offspring’ mean Jesus?

slides.alt_text: Slide two presents the Christian corporate-representation reading of Christ and Abraham's seed.
slides.body: Paul reads all the Abrahamic promises together. They climax in one representative Messiah, and everyone united with Christ becomes Abraham's seed. The one and the many belong together—not as a spelling trick, but as corporate fulfilment.
slides.heading: The strongest Christian case

slides.alt_text: Slide three explains that offspring is a collective singular and classifies Paul's reading as later canonical interpretation.
slides.body: Genesis compares this same ‘offspring’ with uncountable dust and stars. Its singular form normally includes many descendants, so grammar alone cannot identify Jesus. Paul offers an explicit, serious canonical rereading—not a singular-person prediction hidden in Genesis 12:7.
slides.heading: The noun is singular—and collective
